transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena: All right everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, with Marco our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Priya: Hi this is Priya, Head of Data at StoneBridge.
[00:00:11] Ethan: Ethan here, platform eng.
[00:00:13] Marta: Marta, CISO.
[00:00:15] Marco: Hey all, Marco Diaz, SE. thanks for making time.
[00:00:20] Lena: Great. high level, we wanted to understand your inference needs and whether Dedicated capacity makes sense vs hosted. feel free to jump in.
[00:00:30] Priya: Sure. quick context: we run fraud and KYC models in prod. some are customer-facing, real-time scoring, others are batch enrichment that we run daily and monthly. currently most models run on a mix of cloud-hosted endpoints and a small on-prem infra for sensitive PII.
[00:00:45] Ethan: to add, our latency SLO for real-time fraud is sub-200ms 95th p99-ish we try to keep under 300ms for worst case. batch jobs need throughput during month-end when loads spike.
[00:00:57] Lena: got it. do you have a sense of token volumes or qps?
[00:01:02] Priya: rough numbers: real-time scoring about 80 qps peak, average 25 qps. batch pipelines can generate bursts equivalent to 5k concurrent requests for short windows during statement runs. that's why we ask about burst capacity.
[00:01:18] Marco: thanks, that helps. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools so baseline predictability, plus configurable burst — you can reserve lower steady-state and configure burst to use shared capacity when needed or purchase temporary burst nodes.
[00:01:30] Marta: is the burst on our VPC or does traffic route through Redwood's public control plane?
[00:01:35] Marco: good question. we offer two models: dedicated with private control plane where control plane interactions are over a customer-managed VPC peering — in that mode burst still happens within the same cloud region and can be restricted to your subnet. if you need air-gapped on-prem, we also do private deployments but that changes operations and pricing.
[00:01:52] Marta: okay we likely need private control plane + VPC peering. need to confirm with infra.
[00:01:56] Priya: what's the typical setup for KV cache and batching? we care about warm-starts to keep latency down.
[00:02:02] Marco: our runtime supports KV cache persistence across requests for a given session and intelligent batching. for real-time we use small batch sizes with continuous batching heuristics to meet latency SLOs; for batch jobs you can configure larger batch windows to improve throughput and reduce tokens/sec cost.
[00:02:18] Ethan: any notes on quantization? we want to reduce GPU cost but worried about quality regressions on our NLU intents model.
[00:02:24] Marco: we have quantization profiles that Red wood recommends based on workload. some models tolerate int8 very well; others less so. we usually run a small eval set — we can quantize and compare QA metrics and latency/cost tradeoffs during the benchmark.
[00:02:39] Priya: that would be helpful.
[00:02:42] Lena: timeline? are you evaluating now for a Q2 pilot?
[00:02:46] Priya: yes, we want a pilot in April and go live in late Q2 if pilot goes well. budget cycle aligns with that.
[00:02:53] Lena: perfect. can you walk us through stakeholders?
[00:02:56] Priya: contact map: me (product/data), Ethan for infra and sample uploads, Marta for security and compliance sign-off. finance will review pricing after we see projected unit costs.
[00:03:07] Marco: on pricing, we have reserved capacity tiers plus optional burst packs. we can send the worksheet.
[00:03:13] Ethan: two infra constraints: we need SSO/SAML integration and KMS for key management. also outbound egress control — the instances must not phone home to arbitrary endpoints.
[00:03:23] Marco: we support SAML SSO and RBAC. for KMS we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for data-at-rest encryption keys and we can restrict egress — we'd share architecture for VPC peering setup.
[00:03:33] Marta: SOC 2? any audit logs for model access and per-request logs?
[00:03:37] Lena: yes we have SOC 2 and provide audit logs at token/request granularity; can provide retention options. we also support customer-managed audit logging to their splunk/ELK.
[00:03:47] Priya: perfect. for the benchmark, we want to measure p50/p95/p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens for a few models — a smaller transformer for intents and a medium LLM for enrichment. can you run that?
[00:03:58] Marco: absolutely. if you can upload sample prompts and an eval set, we'll run runs on dedicated pools with and without quantization and show throughput and latency numbers.
[00:04:08] Priya: ok I'll get the sample set to you, is S3 ok? we can't put PII in that bucket, so we'll anonymize.
[00:04:14] Marco: S3 is fine, or we can accept a secure upload to your VPC if you prefer. we'll provide the upload instructions.
[00:04:20] Ethan: about scaling: do you support autoscaling within dedicated pools? we want to scale up GPU nodes during business hours and down at night, but keep steady capacity for baseline latency.
[00:04:29] Marco: yes, autoscaling policies can be configured by queue depth and latency SLOs. you can set min/max pool sizes and burst policies. for month-end we recommend a scheduled increase or a burst pack to guarantee capacity.
[00:04:41] Priya: cost visibility is critical. can we get token-level cost breakdown per route in the console?
[00:04:46] Lena: Redwood Console provides per-route and per-model cost breakdowns, token-level slices, and tracing hooks. we'll show the dashboard in follow-up demo.
[00:04:55] Marta: data residency question: some customers require data not leave EU. we have EU customers; can dedicated pools be region-restricted?
[00:05:01] Marco: yes you can pin capacity to regions, and private deployments can be in-region. we'll note region constraints in the worksheet.
[00:05:08] Priya: any runbooks or SLAs for failovers? what happens if a reserved pool becomes unhealthy?
[00:05:14] Marco: we provide health monitoring and automatic fallback policies — traffic can failover to an alternate compatible model or region if configured; for strict isolation you can configure multi-az pools. SLAs are part of Dedicated contracts.
[00:05:26] Ethan: curious about model variants and fallbacks — can we pin a production variant and have a cheaper fallback automatically?
[00:05:31] Marco: yes, routing policies can specify a primary model and fallback variants; that avoids downtime and helps cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:05:36] Priya: great. any gotchas on network for VPC peering and throughput? we do heavy batch uploads during month-end and worried about egress bottlenecks.
[00:05:44] Marco: for high-throughput batch we recommend having antennas — sorry, I mean dedicated VPC bandwidth and analytics for throughput. we also support colocated storage options and allow direct S3 access from the pool. we'll share network config recommendations. (note: transcription sometimes says 'antennas' instead of 'attendant' — sorry.)
[00:05:59] Lena: (laughs) noted.
[00:06:02] Marta: compliance checklist — can you email the SOC 2 report and a list of subprocessor locations?
[00:06:07] Lena: yes we'll attach SOC2 and list of subprocessors.
[00:06:10] Priya: last thing, what's the onboarding time for Dedicated? we can't have a multi-week lead without visibility.
[00:06:15] Marco: typical onboarding for Dedicated with private control plane is 2-4 weeks once contract and infra approvals are in place — pilot can be faster if we start on hosted then migrate.
[00:06:25] Priya: ok we prefer to start pilot on Dedicated to test autoscaling and burst.
[00:06:30] Lena: perfect. we'll send the worksheet and SOC2, Marco will share benchmark plan and upload instructions, Marta will send compliance questions, and Priya will share eval data.
[00:06:39] Ethan: one operational question: will we get token-level logs to our SIEM? and retention windows?
[00:06:44] Marco: yes, we can stream logs to your SIEM with configurable retention; default is 90 days but can be extended.
[00:06:50] Priya: sounds good. any competitors we should watch for?
[00:06:53] Lena: customers often evaluate Anthropic/Anthropic's endpoints or OpenAI for hosted simplicity, and Replicate or self-hosted stacks for control. Redwood differentiates on predictable Dedicated SLOs and private control plane options.
[00:07:05] Marta: thanks.
[00:07:08] Lena: ok we'll recap next steps.
[00:07:11] Marco: Recap: we'll run a benchmark on dedicated pools with and without quantization, send network config notes, and provide pricing worksheet.
[00:07:18] Priya: thanks everyone. we'll aim to get sample set by Friday.
[00:07:22] Lena: thanks, end call.
